identity.trade: Ore and coal: Skarholm's shafts feed the vale's forges, and the carters leave heavy and come back light.

greeting: The shift bell is the only law in the pit. Mind it.
Skarholm is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Foremen are quitting. Not for money. For sleep.
A lamp flame leaned sideways in a sealed gallery. There is a draught from somewhere with no door.
A carter says the ore wagons weigh more going out than they did coming in.

opinions.pernel_larkspur: I would trust Pernel with a purse. A small one.

time.morning: Shift is up. Bring a lamp, bring a prayer.

dialogue.aside: Punctual as ever. I would say a pun-ctual friend, but you heard it last time.

greeting: Sit anywhere that is not wet. The wet ones are the regulars.
Lamp up and mind the timber. We say it twice and mean it.
rumour: Miners drink quick and tip slow. I water the first and ignore the second.
The cellar is cold and the cellar is empty. I ordered more. The order came back as promises.
Pit props are failing on the third level. The foreman says rot. The crew says a knock.
Ask anyone in Skarholm about the Skarholm Ore Yard. You will get four stories and one fact.

opinions.mags_cragg: Mags has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Mags.

time.evening: Shift is done. Wash the dust off, if the water allows.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. I would say nice day, but it is not, and you would know.

greeting: Bring iron or bring coin. Preferably iron.
Skarholm is ore and coal. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Picks wear out in a week and wedges in a day. I keep a pile ready.
The forge hums when the stones dim. Not loud. Enough to notice.
The mine cat will not go below the second level. He is the best judge of air we have.

opinions.evelyn_skerrit: Evelyn undercuts me. I forgive Evelyn. Mostly.
opinions.pernel_larkspur: Pernel has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Pernel.

time.night: Night shift. Keep your voice low. The rock listens.

dialogue.aside: Excuse the dust. Work does not stop for friends, though it does pause.

greeting: Everything has a price. Some of it is even written down.
You will hear Skarholm before you see it. Ask at the Skarholm Ore Yard.
rumour: Candles, picks, tallow. Everything is bought by the dozen and burned by dusk.
Candles are short this month. The wax comes late, and so does the honest news.
Strange scratches on the tunnel wall, above head height. We stopped the dig.
Ask in Skarholm who built the Skarholm Ore Yard and you will get a different name each time.

opinions.kit_seam: I would trust Kit with a purse. A small one.
opinions.mags_cragg: Mags undercuts me. I forgive Mags. Mostly.

time.rain: Rain. The pit floods and the pumps groan. Everybody bails.

dialogue.aside: Argh! Oh, it is you. Sorry. The kettle and I had words. Sit.

greeting: Sit by me. My knees insist.
First time in Skarholm? The Skarholm Ore Yard is the place to start.
rumour: The old stones had names. Nobody writes them down. Nobody asks me.
The pit ponies shy at the same turning every shift. The foreman has stopped using that turning.
The yard boss keeps a lantern burning for the miners who did not come up.

opinions.pernel_larkspur: Pernel keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.morning: Shift is up. Bring a lamp, bring a prayer.

dialogue.aside: Good to see you. Now, what do you need, and what can you spare?

greeting: Stand back from the heat. It does not like being looked at.
The Skarholm Ore Yard is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: The furnace draws like a bellows even when the bellows rest. I check the flue twice a day.
The ore carts run late. The road is fine. The carters are afraid.

opinions.blythe_lambert: Blythe knows the trade. I will say that for Blythe.

time.evening: Shift is done. Wash the dust off, if the water allows.

dialogue.aside: You look rough. Eat something. That is not advice, it is an order.

greeting: Mind the dust. It is in the lungs by dusk.
Strangers in Skarholm get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: The price of coal is up and wages are not. The carts leave fuller each week.
A new shaft hit water and nobody could stop it. The water was warm.
Skarholm iron rings a different note. Smiths can tell.

opinions.dalla_clay: Dalla works hard and talks harder.
opinions.helm_tallis: Helm knows the trade. I will say that for Helm.

time.night: Night shift. Keep your voice low. The rock listens.

dialogue.aside: Look what the wind dragged in. Sit. Do not touch the pie.

greeting: Ore in, iron out, patience in between.
Dust is the town's second weather. Mind your lungs.
rumour: Slag came out glassy last week. Never seen that. The foreman waved it off.
Pay day was delayed and nobody complained. When miners stop complaining, worry.
Whatever you hear about Skarholm, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.eorl_greaves: Eorl knows the trade. I will say that for Eorl.
opinions.helm_tallis: Helm works hard and talks harder.

time.rain: Rain. The pit floods and the pumps groan. Everybody bails.

dialogue.aside: Come in, sit, eat. I will hear no argument.

greeting: Hold the mule. He is not as bad as he looks.
You look clean. Give it an hour.
rumour: Wolves tracked a cart for two miles last week. I counted the miles, not the wolves.
The rock dust has a taste lately. Sweet, like iron and old pennies.

opinions.bartle_eastman: Bartle works hard and talks harder.
opinions.blythe_lambert: Blythe knows the trade. I will say that for Blythe.

time.morning: Shift is up. Bring a lamp, bring a prayer.

dialogue.aside: Punctual as ever. I would say a pun-ctual friend, but you heard it last time.

greeting: Day work, day pay. What is it?
Welcome to Skarholm. Mind the Skarholm Ore Yard. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Dug a drain and hit a flat stone with marks on it. The foreman said fill it in. I did.
The deepest miner swears the rock breathes. He is not drunk, which is the worrying part.
Folk say Skarholm was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

opinions.rafe_farrow: Rafe works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Shift is done. Wash the dust off, if the water allows.

dialogue.aside: There you are. I was just thinking of you, which is rare, and a compliment.

greeting: Mind the lamp. Mind the roof. Mind me.
Folk come to Skarholm for ore and coal. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: The north shaft is shut again. The foreman says the roof. The miners say not.
Skarholm lives by ore and coal. When that fails, so do we.

opinions.bartle_eastman: Bartle works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Night shift. Keep your voice low. The rock listens.

dialogue.aside: Ha! Friend! Pull up a stool, I have a story and half a loaf.

greeting: Lamp up, helmet down. We talk later.
rumour: The roof sang at dawn, a low note. Everyone stopped. Then everyone went back to work.
A stranger asked at the Skarholm Ore Yard for the oldest person in Skarholm. We sent him to the wrong house, on purpose.

opinions.derwin_coldwell: Derwin works hard and talks harder.
opinions.erwin_farrow: Erwin and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

time.rain: Rain. The pit floods and the pumps groan. Everybody bails.

dialogue.aside: Whatever you need, friend. Ask. I will not make you ask twice.

greeting: Coal dust never leaves. Not the lungs, not the stew.
rumour: A tunnel we closed in spring was open this morning. Nobody dug it.
The Skarholm Ore Yard was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.bartle_eastman: Bartle works hard and talks harder.
opinions.derwin_coldwell: Derwin keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.morning: Shift is up. Bring a lamp, bring a prayer.

dialogue.aside: I dreamed of you last night. You were a heron. It suited you.

greeting: Mind the lamp. Mind the roof. Mind me.
rumour: Something knocks back when you knock on the deep face.
Every few years Skarholm has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

opinions.eorl_greaves: Eorl keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.rafe_farrow: Rafe works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Shift is done. Wash the dust off, if the water allows.

dialogue.aside: I do not say this often. It is good to see a face I do not need to avoid.

greeting: I am not lost. I am exploring.
rumour: Mum says do not go past the last post. I am only going to the one before it.
The deepest miner swears the rock breathes. He is not drunk, which is the worrying part.

opinions.rafe_farrow: Rafe and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

clues.note: A survey stone sits a hand's width from its mark. The old socket is clean.
A pit prop charred at the foot. Someone lit a small fire and stamped it out.
A chain cut clean with a good tool and wrapped to look whole.

stashes.say: You drag four trimmed blocks onto the barrow.
